title: Pricing case: a halal energy-drink start-up, and justify frame
subject: Business
source: Written for business/y11 lesson 36 (Pupil PDF worksheet: pricing case and justify frame)
intro: Lesson 36. Read the case and the data, then justify one pricing strategy.

passage.title: Quwwa Drinks
paras: Quwwa Drinks is a new business making a halal-certified energy drink with no artificial colours. It will sell through corner shops and online, aimed at 16 to 25 year olds.
The market is dominated by two big brands with strong loyalty. The owners must choose between penetration pricing (a low launch price) and competitive pricing (the same as rivals).
passage.source: All businesses, people and figures in this case are fictional, made up for practice.

blocks.text: Justify whether Quwwa Drinks should use penetration pricing or competitive pricing. (9 marks)

frame.label: Because (use the data)
frame.prompt: Give a reason and develop it into a chain, using figures from the case.

frame.label: However (the other option)
frame.prompt: Give the strongest point for the other option and develop it.

frame.label: Overall, why my choice beats it
frame.prompt: Compare the two: why your option is better for THIS business.

markScheme.a: Penetration: 64% would try it at £1.10 against 28% at £1.50, which helps a new brand break brand loyalty; margin still £0.25 a can. Competitive: margin £0.65 a can, but few will switch from loyal brands. Judgement must compare, e.g. penetration first then raise the price once loyal. Level 3 (7-9): a justified choice that uses the data, with developed chains of reasoning and a comparison showing why it beats the other option. Level 2 (4-6): reasons for the choice in context but little comparison. Level 1 (1-3): generic points.
